perf_defaults.note: Per-problem overrides live in problems/<id>/config.json 'perf' {min,max,count?,spacing?,jitter?}. The judge samples 'count' geometrically-spaced inputs in [min,max], clamped to distinct integers. When PERF_SEED is set (the hidden official inputs), each point is jittered by up to ±'jitter'; with no seed the points are deterministic (local dev). Contestants know the policy (scale), not the exact hidden n.

timing.note: Local dev uses wall_time. The Linux evaluation host sets metric to 'perf_instructions' (perf stat -e instructions); the median instruction count at each input is the score, reproducible on the fixed host and toolchain (not literally hardware-independent). Submissions are ranked by scaling reach first (largest completed input), then by instruction count at that input.

sandbox.note: 'none' = local dev via the landrun pass-through shim (NO sandboxing). 'container' asserts a real landrun is present and is set by the Docker image. Resource/isolation limits (memory, cpus, pids, network, non-root, kill-all-on-exit) are ENFORCED BY THE CONTAINER RUNTIME, not the judge process — see the docker run flags in the Dockerfile header.
